extracted.intended_audience: general readers, potential contributors, and supporters of Vox (news consumers, journalists, and prospective members)
extracted.subtask_description: Vox's newsroom guiding principles for producing explanatory journalism: audience-first, transparent, evidence-backed reporting that makes complex ideas accessible and useful. These standards cover tone, sourcing, scope, and ethical habits the outlet expects of its journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience-centered
rubrics_metrics.description: Our audience is at the heart of everything we do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We’re not focused on serving people in power — we’re focused on serving you, our audience. We want you to walk away from a Vox story and feel like you’ve learned something new, or understand a topic more deeply. Major events impact real people’s lives; keep that impact in view.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain what matters and how to think about it
rubrics_metrics.description: Vox helps you understand what matters. We tell them what truly matters and how to think about it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The goal is to give readers context and a way to think about a topic, not just raw facts. Reporting should connect facts to meaning and interpretation so readers can form their own judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thorough research and sourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: We do the work — sift through information, read the studies, talk to experts, and gather a range of perspectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting should involve reading studies, consulting subject-matter experts, and assembling multiple perspectives. ‘Show your work’—be explicit about methods and sources so readers can evaluate the reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid sensationalism / panic-inducing headlines
rubrics_metrics.description: We don’t drown you in panic-inducing headlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid fear-driven framing and sensational language. Prioritize accuracy and calm explanation over click-driven alarmism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Helpfulness over speed
rubrics_metrics.description: We’re not obsessed with being the first to break the news; we’re focused on being helpful to you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority is delivering clarity, insight, and useful tools rather than racing to publish first. Accuracy, context, and usefulness can trump speed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility across audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Our journalism is written and produced to be accessible to all, whether you’re a subject-matter expert or hearing about something for the very first time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write and produce with layered explanation so both novices and experts can benefit. Avoid unnecessary jargon and provide clear definitions and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover urgent and neglected stories
rubrics_metrics.description: We report urgently and thoroughly on the most important stories shaping our world, but also on issues the rest of the media neglects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance coverage between high-impact, time-sensitive events and underreported topics. Don’t ignore issues because they aren’t fashionable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer ideas and solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: We explain some of the biggest challenges humanity faces, but we also offer ideas and solutions to confront them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond diagnosis, journalism should surface possible responses, policy options, or practical steps readers can consider—while making clear trade-offs and uncertainties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and showing work
rubrics_metrics.description: Transparency builds trust. We’re transparent about the process, clear about our views, and always show our work, so that you can form your own opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge how reporting was done, disclose methods and limitations, be explicit about editorial stance where relevant, and provide source documentation or links when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge and manage biases; be fair and empathetic
rubrics_metrics.description: We accept that journalists have their own biases — and must be aware of them. We work hard to acknowledge our biases, and be fair and empathetic to all perspectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practices should include self-awareness of bias, deliberate efforts at fairness, and empathetic treatment of people and viewpoints, not false balance but genuine engagement with differing perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity is central; use diverse sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Identity-related topics touch every part of our culture and society, and should be addressed as such. Talking to a diverse array of sources and understanding a variety of perspectives is essential in delivering the right stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat identity dimensions (race, gender, class, etc.) as relevant across beats. Seek diverse voices and sources to avoid blind spots and to surface lived experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don’t start with foregone conclusions; put facts first
rubrics_metrics.description: We don’t start with foregone conclusions. We’re not afraid to make a bold statement backed by expertise and reporting... but we put facts first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid confirming a narrative you set in advance. It is acceptable to make assertive claims, but they must be supported by reporting and evidence; explore other points of view with generosity and fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanatory journalism as a public good
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanatory journalism is a public good. We believe that when more people understand why something is happening, we’re all better off.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat explanatory reporting as civic service—prioritize clarity and pedagogy that helps communities and institutions function better.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide clarity, insight, and practical tools
rubrics_metrics.description: We offer clarity, insight, and tools to help you live a better life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories should aim to be useful: give readers actionable takeaways, frameworks for understanding, or resources they can use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engaging, human tone (have fun)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain an engaging, human voice where appropriate; make journalism readable and enjoyable without sacrificing rigor.
